from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialization
        title = "The Mathematical Playground: The Complex Plane"
        # Removed $ symbols to avoid LaTeX requirement and literal display of '$'
        lines = [
            "Real numbers live on a horizontal line.",
            "Imaginary numbers create a new vertical dimension.",
            "Multiplying by i rotates your position 90 degrees."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Pivot point (Origin) at D3 for the coordinate system
        origin_pos = self.grid['D3']
        pos_1 = self.grid['D4'] # 1 unit to the right
        pos_i = self.grid['C3'] # 1 unit up

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Color match: Line 1 text is White, Real axis is White
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        real_axis = Line(start=self.grid['D1'], end=self.grid['D6'], color=WHITE)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to resolve "latex" not found error
        real_label = Text("Real", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(real_label, "D6").shift(DOWN * 0.4)
        
        self.play(Create(real_axis), Write(real_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Color match: Line 2 text is White, Imaginary axis is White
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        imag_axis = Line(start=self.grid['F3'], end=self.grid['A3'], color=WHITE)
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to resolve "latex" not found error
        imag_label = Text("Imaginary", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(imag_label, "A3").shift(LEFT * 0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(imag_axis), Write(imag_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Color match: Line 3 text is Magenta to match the rotation arc
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # Position '1' on Real axis
        dot_1 = Dot(pos_1, color="#00FF00")
        label_1 = Text("1", font_size=24, color="#00FF00").next_to(dot_1, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Position 'i' on Imaginary axis
        dot_i = Dot(pos_i, color="#00FFFF")
        # Added slant=ITALIC to denote variable 'i'
        label_i = Text("i", font_size=24, slant=ITALIC, color="#00FFFF").next_to(dot_i, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Rotation arc
        rotation_arc = Arc(
            radius=1.0,
            start_angle=0,
            angle=PI/2,
            arc_center=origin_pos,
            color="#FF00FF"
        )
        
        # Step-by-step display
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_1), Write(label_1))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Create(rotation_arc), run_time=1.2)
        
        # Animate the transition representing the multiplication by i
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(dot_1, rotation_arc),
            FadeIn(dot_i),
            Write(label_i),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout
        self.setup_layout(

            [

            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), run_time=0.5)
        
        # Display the constant 'e' in green
        e_val_text = Text("e ≈ 2.718", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(e_val_text, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(e_val_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second line in White (default is white, but ensure visibility)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.5)
        
        # Show a real line and the origin
        origin_pt = self.grid["D1"]
        end_pt = self.grid["D6"]
        real_axis = Line(origin_pt, end_pt, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        origin_marker = Dot(origin_pt, color=WHITE, radius=0.08)
        origin_label = Text("0", font_size=18).next_to(origin_marker, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Tracker for the growth vector length
        v_length = ValueTracker(0.01)
        
        # Vector on the real line
        growth_vec = Arrow(
            start=origin_pt,
            end=origin_pt + RIGHT * 0.1,
            buff=0,
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=5,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.3
        )
        
        # Simple updater for length
        growth_vec.add_updater(
            lambda m: m.put_start_and_end_on(
                origin_pt, 
                origin_pt + RIGHT * v_length.get_value()
            )
        )
        
        self.play(Create(real_axis), FadeIn(origin_marker), FadeIn(origin_label))
        self.add(growth_vec)
        
        # Initial growth from origin
        self.play(v_length.animate.set_value(1.5), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third line in Yellow
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)

        self.play(
            FadeIn(ex_label),
            growth_vec.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        # Continuous acceleration (exponential feel)
        # Vector expands to cover more of the line
        self.play(
            v_length.animate.set_value(4.5),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=rush_into  # Provides acceleration feel
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup context
        title = "The Twist: Imaginary Growth as Rotation"
        lines = [
            "What happens if growth is multiplied by i?",
            "The growth force now acts at a right angle.",
            "Instead of pushing away, it pulls into a turn.",
            "Continuous sideways growth creates a perfect circular path.",
            "This is the origin of the unit circle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        formula = Text("e^ix", font_size=48, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "A3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        center_pos = self.grid["D4"]
        radius = 1.8
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=radius, color="#555555", stroke_width=2)
        unit_circle.move_to(center_pos)
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(formula),
            Create(unit_circle),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        theta = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def get_radial_pos():
            t = theta.get_value()
            return center_pos + radius * np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), 0])
        
        def get_radial_vector():
            t = theta.get_value()
            direction = np.array([np.cos(t), np.sin(t), 0])
            start = center_pos # Show growth from center to point
            end = get_radial_pos()
            return Arrow(start, end, color="#00FF00", buff=0, tip_length=0.2)

        growth_vec = always_redraw(get_radial_vector)
        self.play(Create(growth_vec), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        def get_perp_vector():
            t = theta.get_value()
            tangent_dir = np.array([-np.sin(t), np.cos(t), 0])
            start = get_radial_pos()
            end = start + tangent_dir * 1.2
            return Arrow(start, end, color="#00FFFF", buff=0, tip_length=0.2)

        perp_vec = always_redraw(get_perp_vector)
        self.play(Create(perp_vec), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(get_radial_pos(), color=YELLOW))
        path = TracedPath(dot.get_center, dissipating_time=2, stroke_width=4, color=YELLOW)
        
        self.add(dot, path)
        self.play(
            theta.animate.set_value(TAU),
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        highlight_circle = Circle(radius=radius, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        highlight_circle.move_to(center_pos)
        
        self.play(
            Create(highlight_circle),
            formula.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(YELLOW),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Plane
        # Replacing ComplexPlane with NumberPlane and using label_constructor=Text.
        # ComplexPlane triggers a LaTeX 'latex' call for the imaginary unit 'i' even when 
        # label_constructor=Text is passed, because of internal unit handling in DecimalNumber.
        # NumberPlane avoids this internal LaTeX-dependent unit logic.
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": BLUE_D,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.5
            }
        ).add_coordinates(label_constructor=Text)

        # 2. Title and Formula
        # Using Text to bypass the 'latex' command requirement
        title = Text("e^iθ = cos(θ) + i sin(θ)", font_size=36).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(Create(plane))

        # 3. Trackers and Logic
        x_tracker = ValueTracker(0)

        def get_current_point():
            val = x_tracker.get_value()
            # Calculate coordinates manually using Euler's formula: e^(i*theta) = cos(theta) + i*sin(theta)
            real_part = np.cos(val)
            imag_part = np.sin(val)
            return plane.coords_to_point(real_part, imag_part)

        # 4. Animated Elements
        moving_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW, radius=0.08)
        moving_dot.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(get_current_point()))

        radius_line = always_redraw(
            lambda: Line(
                start=plane.coords_to_point(0, 0),
                end=get_current_point(),
                stroke_width=4,
                color=YELLOW_A
            )
        )

        trace_arc = always_redraw(
            lambda: Arc(
                radius=plane.get_x_unit_size(),
                start_angle=0,
                angle=x_tracker.get_value(),
                color=YELLOW,
                stroke_width=5
            )
        )

        # Angle Label using Text with basic unicode support
        angle_label = always_redraw(
            lambda: Text(
                f"θ = {x_tracker.get_value() / PI:.2f}π",
                color=YELLOW,
                font_size=24
            ).next_to(moving_dot, UR, buff=0.2)
        )

        # 5. Animation Sequence
        self.add(radius_line, trace_arc, moving_dot, angle_label)
        
        self.play(
            x_tracker.animate.set_value(PI),
            run_time=6,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 6. Conclusion: Euler's Identity
        # Using Text to ensure successful rendering without a LaTeX installation
        euler_identity = Text("e^iπ = -1", color=YELLOW).scale(1.8)
        euler_identity.add_background_rectangle()
        euler_identity.to_edge(DOWN, buff=1)

        self.play(
            Indicate(moving_dot, scale_factor=2),
            Write(euler_identity)
        )
        self.play(euler_identity.animate.set_color(GOLD))
        
        self.wait(3)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        title_text = "The Grand Finale: e^(i*pi) = -1"
        lecture_lines = [
            'Let the growth continue for a distance of pi.',
            'This path takes us halfway around the unit circle.',
            'We started at positive 1 on the real axis.',
            'After a pi rotation, we reach the opposite side.',
            'We have arrived exactly at negative 1.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Pre-define visual elements ===
        
        # 1. Formula substitution
        formula_sub = Text("e^(i*pi) = cos(pi) + i sin(pi)", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(formula_sub, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.7)

        # 2. Complex Plane visual
        plane_center = self.grid["D4"]
        axes = ComplexPlane(
            x_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": GREY_B}
        ).move_to(plane_center)
        
        unit_circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=GREY_D).move_to(plane_center)
        
        # Vector and Arc logic
        vec_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        vector = always_redraw(lambda: Arrow(
            start=plane_center,
            end=plane_center + np.array([np.cos(vec_tracker.get_value()), np.sin(vec_tracker.get_value()), 0]) * 1.5,
            buff=0,
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=4
        ))
        
        arc = always_redraw(lambda: Arc(
            radius=1.5,
            start_angle=0,
            angle=vec_tracker.get_value(),
            color="#FFFF00",
            stroke_width=5
        ).shift(plane_center))

        # 3. Points and Labels
        start_dot = Dot(plane_center + RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE)
        start_label = Text("1", font_size=20).next_to(start_dot, DR, buff=0.1)
        
        end_dot = Dot(plane_center + LEFT * 1.5, color=RED)
        end_label = Text("-1", font_size=20).next_to(end_dot, DL, buff=0.1)

        # Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(formula_sub))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(unit_circle))
        self.play(FadeIn(start_dot), Write(start_label))
        
        self.add(vector, arc)
        self.play(vec_tracker.animate.set_value(PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(end_dot), Write(end_label))
        
        # Conclusion text
        conclusion = Text("e^(i*pi) = -1", color=YELLOW, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(conclusion, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(conclusion))
        
        self.wait(3)

        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define the equations as Text objects
        # In Manim CE, Text objects are VGroups of characters, allowing index-based access
        # e^iπ+1=0 -> indices: e(0), ^(1), i(2), π(3), +(4), 1(5), =(6), 0(7)
        equation_v1 = Text("e^iπ+1=0")
        
        # e^iπ=-1 -> indices: e(0), ^(1), i(2), π(3), =(4), -(5), 1(6)
        equation_v2 = Text("e^iπ=-1")

        # Applying colors via character indexing as requested
        # Using common mathematical color coding
        equation_v1[0].set_color(YELLOW)  # e
        equation_v1[2].set_color(BLUE)    # i
        equation_v1[3].set_color(GREEN)   # π
        equation_v1[5].set_color(WHITE)   # 1
        equation_v1[7].set_color(WHITE)   # 0
        
        # Matching colors for equation_v2
        equation_v2[0].set_color(YELLOW)  # e
        equation_v2[2].set_color(BLUE)    # i
        equation_v2[3].set_color(GREEN)   # π
        equation_v2[6].set_color(WHITE)   # 1

        # Positioning both equations in the specified grid area "B2" to "D5"
        self.place_in_area(equation_v1, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.place_in_area(equation_v2, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.5)

        # Initial Animation: Display the first form of the identity
        self.play(Write(equation_v1))
        self.wait(1)

        # Transform matching shapes between the two versions of the equation
        # TransformMatchingShapes is ideal for Text/VMobjects with similar components
        self.play(
            TransformMatchingShapes(equation_v1, equation_v2),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unveiling Euler's Identity: The Bridge Between Algebra and Geometry
outline.target_audience: Late high school students or early university undergraduates (STEM focused)

sections.title: The Mathematical Playground: The Complex Plane
sections.content: Introduce the prerequisite concept of the Complex Plane. Explain that while real numbers live on a horizontal line, imaginary numbers ($i$) create a vertical dimension. Visualize the 2D coordinate system where the x-axis is 'Real' and the y-axis is 'Imaginary'.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Math-Ant' starting at the number 1 on the horizontal line. If we multiply the Ant's position by $i$, the Ant doesn't move further right; it performs a 90-degree left turn to land on $i$ in the vertical dimension.

sections.title: The Meaning of 'e': Continuous Growth
sections.content: Define $e$ (approx. 2.718) as the base of natural growth. Explain that $e^x$ represents a process where growth is compounded continuously. Use a vector arrow to show that in the real world, $e^x$ pushes a point away from the origin along the real line.
sections.example: Think of a 'Growth-Bot' that always moves in the direction it is facing. In real numbers, it accelerates straight ahead, getting faster and further away from home (zero) every second.

sections.title: The Twist: Imaginary Growth as Rotation
sections.content: Introduce the core of Euler's Formula: $e^{ix}$. Explain that when the 'growth' is multiplied by $i$ (the imaginary unit), the force of growth is applied at a 90-degree angle to the current position. This change in direction turns 'pushing away' into 'turning around'.
sections.example: Picture the Growth-Bot again, but now its steering wheel is locked at a 90-degree angle. Instead of flying off into infinity, the bot is forced to drive in a perfect circle around the origin (the Unit Circle).

sections.title: Connecting the Dots: Euler's Formula Visualized
sections.content: Present the formula $e^{ix} = \cos(x) + i\sin(x)$. Explain that $x$ represents the 'distance' or 'angle' traveled along the circle. Use an animated unit circle to show how any point on the circle is a mix of a horizontal (cosine) and vertical (sine) component.
sections.example: If the Growth-Bot travels for a 'time' of $x = \pi/2$ (90 degrees), the formula shows its position is $0 + 1i$. It has moved from the 'Real' 1 to the 'Imaginary' $i$.

sections.title: The Grand Finale: $e^{i\pi} = -1$
sections.content: Apply the logic to the specific case where $x = \pi$. Since $\pi$ is the distance halfway around a circle, the Growth-Bot travels from the starting point (1) to the exact opposite side of the origin. This lands the bot at -1 on the real axis.
sections.example: The Math-Ant walks a path of length $\pi$ along the circular track. After completing exactly half the circle, it looks down and realizes it is standing on the number -1. This connects $e$, $i$, and $\pi$ in one elegant move.

sections.title: Summary: The Most Beautiful Equation
sections.content: Conclude by rearranging the identity to $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$. Highlight how this single equation unites the five most important constants in mathematics: 0, 1, $e$, $i$, and $\pi$.
sections.example: Imagine five different species (Arithmetic, Calculus, Geometry, Algebra, and Trigonometry) coming together to build a single bridge. This equation is that bridge.

storyboard.title: The Mathematical Playground: The Complex Plane
lecture_lines: Real numbers live on a horizontal number line.
Imaginary numbers create a new, vertical dimension.
We start at the number one on the real axis.
Imaginary unit $i$ sits on the vertical axis.
Multiplying by $i$ rotates our position by 90 degrees.
animations: Draw a horizontal 'Real' number line in white (#FFFFFF) and incorporate the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/based.svg] icon to represent the foundation.

Place a bright green dot at the number 1 on the Real axis (#00FF00).
Place a cyan dot at the number 'i' on the Imaginary axis (#00FFFF).
Animate a magenta arc (#FF00FF) rotating the green dot 90 degrees to the cyan 'i'.

storyboard.title: The Meaning of 'e': Continuous Growth
lecture_lines: The number $e$ represents continuous, natural growth.
This growth pushes values away from the origin.
It accelerates straight ahead along the real line.
animations: Display the constant 'e' (approx 2.718) in green (#00FF00).
Show a vector on the real line growing continuously to the right.
Label the growth 'e^x' and highlight its outward push in yellow (#FFFF00).

storyboard.title: The Twist: Imaginary Growth as Rotation
lecture_lines: Multiplying growth by $i$ creates a fundamental change.
Now, the growth force acts at a right angle.
This constant sideways push creates a rotation.
Instead of flying away, the point travels in circles.
This continuous turn defines the unit circle.
animations: Display the expression e^{ix} next to a gray unit circle (#555555).
Place a growth vector at (1,0) on the circle in green (#00FF00).
Add a blue perpendicular vector at the tip to show the 'i' effect (#00FFFF).
Animate the growth vector rotating along the circle's circumference.
Trace the circular path in yellow (#FFFF00) as the vector rotates.

storyboard.title: Connecting the Dots: Euler's Formula Visualized
lecture_lines: Euler's formula describes every point on this circle.
The variable $x$ represents the distance traveled.
Cosine and sine track the horizontal and vertical positions.
animations: Write the formula e^{ix} = cos(x) + i*sin(x) in white (#FFFFFF).
Draw a vector at angle 'x' on the unit circle in green (#00FF00).
Show the horizontal (cos) and vertical (sin) projections in red (#FF0000) and blue (#0000FF).

storyboard.title: The Grand Finale: $e^{i\pi} = -1$
lecture_lines: Let the growth continue for a distance of $\pi$.
We travel exactly halfway around the circle.
We end up on the opposite side of one.
This path of length $\pi$ leads to negative one.
We have arrived at the identity $e^{i\pi} = -1$.
animations: Update the formula to substitute 'x' with 'pi' (#FFFFFF).
Animate the vector traveling exactly 180 degrees to the left side of the circle.
Highlight the destination point -1 on the real axis in red (#FF0000).
Show the arc length labeled with the symbol 'pi' (#FFFF00).
Display the final identity e^{i*pi} = -1 in bold center white.

storyboard.title: Summary: The Most Beautiful Equation
lecture_lines: We can rearrange this into its most famous form.
It unites the five fundamental constants of mathematics.
This identity bridges algebra, geometry, and calculus together.
animations: Rearrange the equation to e^{i*pi} + 1 = 0 in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight the five constants (e, i, pi, 1, 0) with distinct vibrant colors.
Fade out the background as the camera zooms slowly into the elegant identity.
